question.question: Does adding the Rank-n-Contrast term (lambda 0.007, tau 0.1, unit-normalised pooled embedding of the single training forward, no projection head) to the frozen K1 post-BN 100K recipe improve selected development MAE by at least the frozen 3 meV material gate over a same-run reference from the same initial state?
question.deficiency: Every recorded K1 100K screen changed architecture, optimizer or same-molecule view agreement; none constrained the cross-molecule geometry of the pooled embedding by Gap distance. Rank-n-Contrast (arXiv 2210.01189) did so for image and EEG regression, but its weakest scheme is the joint one used here.
alternatives: The 192-d pooled embedding already orders Gap through the L1 head and the extra geometry constraint only competes with it
Train-mode BatchNorm and dropout make embedding distances too noisy for the contrast to help
A below-gate difference is inside the same-init perturbation floor
question.positive_decision: Retain a material lead only if every frozen protocol condition holds; any multi-seed confirmation needs a separate explicit compute decision. No 500K or full training follows.
question.negative_decision: Close Rank-n-Contrast at 100K with no tau, lambda, projection-head or RankSim successor.

profile.cheapest_falsifier: One T4x2 session: same-run reference plus one Rank-n-Contrast arm, one arm per device.
